# The library's methods: what is already there to call

Every method below is declared in `cypress/support/core/`, with exactly these parameters.
**Call only a method you have seen declared**, here or in its class, with arguments of those types:
a call written from memory is the most common way new code fails to compile, and the suite's rules,
which read the sources, cannot see it. When you cannot run `npx tsc --noEmit`, check every call you wrote
against this card before you say you are done, and say that the code was not compiled.

These are where to look first, not a fence. Page code (elements, actions, checks) may also call
`cy` itself when nothing here does what a story needs (a download, a drag, a wait for a
response); a story test never does. The rules read the sources: such a call fails them in a test, not in
page code.

A `PageElement` is a constant of a page's Elements object (`HomeElements.ABOUT_LINK`).

## UserActions

- `UserActions.click(element: PageElement)`: Clicks it.
- `UserActions.clickOpeningNewTab(element: PageElement)`: Clicks a link that opens a new tab. Cypress drives one tab, so the link opens in this one instead (its target is taken off first); the next page object carries on here.
- `UserActions.hover(element: PageElement)`: Points the mouse at it: the events a menu's script listens for. A menu that opens on CSS :hover alone does not open (Cypress can't move a real mouse); click what is in it with clickHidden(), as the header's navigation does.
- `UserActions.clickHidden(element: PageElement)`: Clicks a link a visitor reaches through a menu that only opens on CSS :hover.
- `UserActions.type(element: PageElement, text: string)`: Replaces what is in the field with this text.
- `UserActions.typeSecret(element: PageElement, secret: string)`: Types a password or other secret. The step says a secret was typed, never what it was.
- `UserActions.clear(element: PageElement)`: Empties the field.
- `UserActions.choose(element: PageElement, option: string)`: Chooses an option of a dropdown (a select element) by its value or its visible text.
- `UserActions.attach(element: PageElement, path: string)`: Attaches a file to a file field (input type="file"), by its path from the suite's folder; a file field is never typed into.
- `UserActions.tick(element: PageElement)`: Ticks a checkbox or picks a radio button.
- `UserActions.untick(element: PageElement)`: Unticks a checkbox.
- `UserActions.setTicked(element: PageElement, ticked: boolean)`: Ticks or unticks: what a page's check() and uncheck() actions call.
- `UserActions.pressKey(element: PageElement, key: string)`: Presses a key in it: "Enter", "Escape", "ArrowDown" (Cypress has no Tab key).
- `UserActions.readText(element: PageElement)` returns `Cypress.Chainable<string>`: Reads the text a visitor sees in it, trimmed. The step says what it read.

## Checks

- `Checks.isShown(element: PageElement)`: It is shown.
- `Checks.isNotShown(element: PageElement)`: It is gone, or hidden.
- `Checks.allShown(what: string, ...elements: PageElement[])`: All of them are shown: one step, and the failure names the first one missing.
- `Checks.hasText(element: PageElement, expected: string)`: It says exactly this (runs of spaces and line breaks count as one space).
- `Checks.hasValue(element: PageElement, expected: string)`: A field holds exactly this: what was typed into it.
- `Checks.containsText(element: PageElement, expected: string)`: Its text contains this.
- `Checks.pageShowsText(text: string)`: The page shows this text somewhere a visitor can see it (any case; part of a longer text is fine).
- `Checks.hasCount(what: string, all: Locator, expected: number)`: The page shows this many of them. It takes the locator of all of them, byCss('ul.results > li'), as a page element stands for the first match. Hidden ones (a mobile menu's copies) are not counted.
- `Checks.linksToEach(what: string, hrefs: string[])`: The page shows a link to each of these addresses, by its href as written: a list still leading to every page it led to in the crawl. Fails naming each one gone.
- `Checks.allDifferent(what: string, names: string[], values: string[])`: Each value is its own: no two the same. allDifferent("page types' titles", names, titles) fails naming the two that share one.
- `Checks.clickChangesThePage(label: string, xpath: string)`: Clicks a control the crawl saw on most of the site's pages (a carousel's Next, a "More" toggle), found by its XPath, and checks that the page around it changes: the region it is in, the control itself (aria-expanded), or the page's own classes. Only controls that move or open something are tested this way: nothing is sent.
- `Checks.shownInComponent(label: string, host: string, inside: string[], says: string, why: string)`: A control inside a web component's shadow root (the unstable family): found from its host (an XPath) through each shadow root on the way (a CSS selector each), shown, and saying `says` when it is not empty. Its failure ends with why the test is unstable.
- `Checks.isEnabled(element: PageElement)`: It is shown, and can be used (a button or field that is not disabled).
- `Checks.isDisabled(element: PageElement)`: It is shown, and disabled.
- `Checks.isChecked(element: PageElement)`: A checkbox or radio button is shown, and ticked.
- `Checks.isNotChecked(element: PageElement)`: A checkbox or radio button is shown, and not ticked.
- `Checks.refusesEmpty(element: PageElement)`: The browser will not send the field's form with the field as it is: it is required, empty, and its form leaves the browser's own check on. Asked of the field, never by sending: nothing leaves the browser.
- `Checks.hasAttribute(element: PageElement, name: string, expected: string)`: Its attribute holds exactly this: hasAttribute(HELP_LINK, 'href', '/help').
- `Checks.isOnPath(path: string)`: The browser is on this path of the site.
- `Checks.titleIs(title: string)`: The page's title is exactly this.
- `Checks.assume(met: boolean, why: string)`: What the test needs is there (the data it uses, a state of the site): when it is not, the test is skipped, saying why, never failed. Name the data: `Checks.assume(policies.length > 0, 'no policy with an amount due in policies.csv')`; inside a `.then()` for data Cypress reads. Not a check (SR-19): the test still checks something.
- `Checks.blockedBy(code: string, why: string)`: Where an open bug (bugs/open/<code>.md, filed by Suite Builder from the crawl) breaks the test: the step says so, and the test is blocked by it, a skip naming the bug, not a failure. Inside a `.then()`.
- `Checks.answers(path: string)`: The address answers, and lands where it says (a redirect means the link points to an old or moved address).
- `Checks.linksAnswerAsInTheCrawl(links: [string, number | null, string[]][], expected: [string, number][] = [])`: The link report: every address the crawl requested (support/links.ts: its path, what it answered then, pages linking to it), asked once more, the report in cypress/link-report.md. Fails only on one that answered 2xx in the crawl and does not now; one already broken then is listed as known, never failed again. A link the team lists as expected to fail (`expected`: its path and the status it answers, support/expected-links.ts) is held to that status instead: it fails only when it answers anything else.
- `Checks.externalLinksAnswerAsInTheCrawl(links: [string, number, 'alive' | 'barred' | 'broken', string[]][])`: Every link to another site the crawl got an answer from, asked again (cypress.config.ts, askLinks), the report in cypress/external-link-report.md. Gone: 400 or more, or no answer twice; it fails when the link answered in the crawl. A site that keeps test tools out (401, 403, 429, 999) is never judged; one already broken in the crawl is listed as known; and when example.com gives no answer either, no link without an answer is called gone: the network, not the sites. A link, or a redirect of it, leading further in than the site under test (a private network, this computer) is never asked.
- `Checks.isNotFound(path: string)`: An address that cannot exist answers 404: the site says a missing page is missing.

## WaitActions

- `WaitActions.forUrl(path: string, failure: (url: string) => string)`: The browser is on exactly this path of the site (query and #fragment aside, but for a hash router's route: #/about).
- `WaitActions.forUrlShape(shapes: readonly string[], failure: (url: string) => string)`: A URL of one of these shapes, e.g. "/blog/*": "*" is one path segment, "{n}" a number.
- `WaitActions.forPageLoad()`: Waits up to pageLoadTimeout for the load event without failing; noteIfStillLoading() names a late one. (cy.visit() still fails on it: Cypress's rule.)
- `WaitActions.noteIfStillLoading(name: string)`: After the page is proven: says so if its load event was late, and what it was still loading.
- `WaitActions.forTitle(title: string, failure: (actual: string) => string)`: Exactly this title (runs of whitespace count as one space).
- `WaitActions.forTitleShape(startsWith: string, endsWith: string, failure: (actual: string) => string)`: A title that starts and ends like this (the page's own name goes in between).
- `WaitActions.forVisibilityOf(element: PageElement, failure: string, timeoutMs?: number)`: The element is visible (within timeoutMs, if given).
- `WaitActions.forInvisibilityOf(element: PageElement, failure: string)`: The element is gone or hidden: a spinner, an overlay, a "Loading..." message.
- `WaitActions.isVisibleNow(element: PageElement)` returns `boolean`: True now (no waiting) when the element is visible.
- `WaitActions.samePage(url: string, expectedUrl: string)` returns `boolean`: True when both URLs are the same page: same site and path; query, #fragment and a final "/" aside, but for a hash router's route (#/about).
- `WaitActions.fitsShapes(url: string, shapes: readonly string[])` returns `boolean`: True when the URL's path has one of these shapes.
- `WaitActions.fitsShape(url: string, shape: string)` returns `boolean`: True when the URL's path has this shape: "*" is any one segment, "{n}" a number.
- `WaitActions.sameText(text: string | null | undefined, expected: string)` returns `boolean`: True when both say the same, whatever the spacing: runs of whitespace count as one space.
- `WaitActions.containsText(text: string | null | undefined, expected: string)` returns `boolean`: True when the text contains the expected words, whatever the spacing.
- `WaitActions.titleFits(title: string, startsWith: string, endsWith: string)` returns `boolean`: (no description: read it in its class)

## SiteConfig

- `SiteConfig.baseUrl()` returns `string`: (no description: read it in its class)
- `SiteConfig.url(path: string)` returns `string`: The full URL of a path on the site under test, e.g. url('/about').
- `SiteConfig.secret(name: string)` returns `Cypress.Chainable<string>`: A secret a test needs (a password, an API key), from the environment variable CYPRESS_<name> (or --env name=...), as a Cypress chain: SiteConfig.secret('password').then((password) => UserActions.typeSecret(LoginElements.PASSWORD_INPUT, password)). Fails, saying how to pass it, when it isn't set. Secrets never go into the code, a saved page or a log.
- `SiteConfig.value(name: string, fallback: string)` returns `string`: Test data that may differ between copies of the site (a product on staging): from --expose name=... (or the expose block of cypress.config.ts), else the fallback.

## StepLog

- `StepLog.start()`: Starts a new test's log. The support file calls this before every test.
- `StepLog.step(sentence: string)`: A step the test takes, as a visitor would say it: step('Type the email address').
- `StepLog.note(remark: string)`: A remark that is not a step of its own, e.g. "now on the services page".
- `StepLog.steps()` returns `string[]`: The steps so far, in order.
- `StepLog.reason(error: Error)` returns `string`: Why something failed, in one line: the first line of the message, without Cypress's "Timed out retrying" prefix. A page or address that did not answer says which, and the network's own error: "`cy.visit()` could not load https://x.test/contact/: connect ETIMEDOUT 192.0.2.1:443", where Cypress's first line ends at "failed trying to load:". An address that took no connection is named, with how to see the others: Cypress tries one address, where a browser tries the next.
- `StepLog.failure(error: Error)` returns `string`: What is printed when a test fails: the step it failed at, and why.
